facts.quote: A tyrannosauroid theropod.

facts.statement: Larsonvenator was described by Sancarlo and Paul.
facts.quote: Authors: Sancarlo & Paul

facts.statement: Larsonvenator lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) age.
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: The type locality of Larsonvenator is the Hell Creek Formation.

facts.statement: Larsonvenator fossils have been found in the United States.
facts.quote: Country: United States

facts.statement: The taxonomic status of Nanotyrannus has been a subject of intense scientific debate.
facts.quote: Its taxonomic status has since been a subject of intense scientific debate.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus is based on the skull CMNH 7541, collected in 1942 by David Hosbrook Dunkle.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus is based on CMNH 7541, a skull collected in 1942 by David Hosbrook Dunkle.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus was described in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore as a new species of Gorgosaurus.
facts.quote: It was described in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore, who classified it as a new species in the tyrannosaurid genus Gorgosaurus, G. lancensis.

facts.statement: The Nanotyrannus specimen was re-described in 1988 by Robert T. Bakker, Michael Williams, and Phil Currie.
facts.quote: In 1988, the specimen was re-described by Robert T. Bakker, Michael Williams, then the curator of paleontology at the Cleveland Museum of Natural History, and Phil Currie, where the original specimen was housed and is now on display.

facts.statement: Subsequent analysis by Thomas Carr in 1999 indicated the specimen was immature, leading many paleontologists to consider it a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Subsequent analysis of the specimen by Thomas Carr in 1999 indicated that it was immature, leading Carr and many other paleontologists to consider it a juvenile specimen of T. rex.

facts.statement: The Nanotyrannus fossil was acquired by the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences in 2020.
facts.quote: The fossil was acquired by the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences in 2020, after which the museum built an additional research lab space in which to prepare, study, and display the specimens.

facts.statement: Paleontologists Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli published an initial description of the "Bloody Mary" specimen in 2025.
facts.quote: In 2025, paleontologists Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli published an initial description of the "Bloody Mary" specimen as part of an extensive revision of the genus Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lancensis specimens are reported to have 15-16 teeth on the upper jaw and 16-18 on the lower jaw, while adult Tyrannosaurus rex have 11-12 upper and 12-14 lower teeth.
facts.quote: Specimens referred to N. lancensis have 15-16 teeth on each side of the maxilla (upper jaw) and 16-18 teeth on each side of the dentary (lower jaw), whereas adult T. rex specimens had 11–12 tooth positions in the upper jaw and 12–14 in the lower.

facts.statement: Carr hypothesized that Nanotyrannus lancensis is a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex based on a decrease in tooth count during growth observed in Gorgosaurus libratus.
facts.quote: Carr showed that, in Gorgosaurus libratus, the number of teeth decreased as the animal grew, and he used this data to support the hypothesis that N. lancensis is simply a juvenile T. rex.

facts.statement: Tsujihi and colleagues noted that tooth count varies individually in Tyrannosaurus and Gorgosaurus regardless of age, suggesting it may not indicate distinct species.
facts.quote: These researchers also noted, however, that both Tyrannosaurus and Gorgosaurus show significant differences in tooth count between individuals of the same age group, and that tooth count may vary on an individual basis unrelated to growth.

facts.statement: A 2016 analysis suggested Nanotyrannus specimens show differing levels of cursoriality compared to Tyrannosaurus rex, potentially indicating taxonomic distinction.
facts.quote: A limb proportion analysis published in 2016 suggested that Nanotyrannus specimens have differing levels of cursoriality, cited as a potential difference between N. lancensis and T. rex.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Woodward et al. concluded that Nanotyrannus specimens are immature and likely belong to Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: A 2020 study by Holly N. Woodward and colleagues indicated that the specimens referred to Nanotyrannus are ontogenetically immature and found it probable that these specimens belonged to Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: Yun (2015) claimed that all distinguishing features of Nanotyrannus are due to individual variation, ontogeny, or taphonomic distortion.
facts.quote: Yun (2015) claimed that all of the differences used to distinguish Nanotyrannus were individually or ontogenetically variable features, or the products of taphonomic distortion of the bones.

facts.statement: Longrich and Saitta (2024) suggested Nanotyrannus is a distinct taxon potentially outside Tyrannosauridae based on morphology, ontogeny, and phylogeny.
facts.quote: In 2024, Nicholas Longrich and Evan T. Saitta re-examined the holotype and referred specimens of Nanotyrannus. Based on several factors, including differences in morphology, ontogeny, and phylogeny, Longrich and Saitta suggested that Nanotyrannus is a distinct taxon that may fall outside of Tyrannosauridae, based on some of their phylogenetic analyses.

facts.statement: Voris et al. (2025) argued that Longrich and Saitta's placement of Nanotyrannus outside Tyrannosauridae was due to immaturity-related scoring and data issues, supporting the juvenile T. rex hypothesis.
facts.quote: Voris et al. (June 2025) suggested that the scoring of Nanotyrannus in a more basal position by Longrich & Saitta (2024) may have been caused by "scoring characteristics related to immaturity" and problematic data sets, supporting the previous interpretation that Nanotyrannus represents a juvenile T. rex.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul (June 2025) supported a basal eutyrannosaurian position for Nanotyrannus as part of his "multiple small taxa hypothesis" for theropod diversity.
facts.quote: Later in June 2025, Gregory S. Paul also supported a basal eutyrannosaurian (non-tyrannosaurid) position for Nanotyrannus, emphasizing the validity and distinction of this genus as part of his preferred "multiple small taxa hypothesis" (MSTH) for theropod diversity in the Hell Creek Formation.

facts.statement: Paul argued that N. lancensis is a wastebasket taxon containing fossils of multiple taxa under his MSTH framework.
facts.quote: Based on the MSTH, Paul also argued for the validity of Stygivenator, a Hell Creek theropod known from a fragmentary skull, and claimed that N. lancensis has been treated as a wastebasket taxon that likely comprises fossils of multiple taxa.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli (October 2025) affirmed the validity of Nanotyrannus after re-examining the "Bloody Mary" specimen.
facts.quote: In October 2025, the validity of Nanotyrannus was affirmed in an extensive paper by Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli, in which the "Bloody Mary" specimen (NCSM 40000) was re-examined.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli concluded the "Jane" specimen died between the ages of 8-14 years.
facts.quote: In the same paper, Zanno and Napoli concluded that another Nanotyrannus specimen, Jane (BMRP 2002.4.1), which they assigned to N. lethaeus, died between the ages of 8–14.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli argued that fitting Nanotyrannus into Tyrannosaurus requires an unprecedented ontogeny pattern not seen in archosaurs, contradicting skeletal fusion patterns.
facts.quote: For these specimens to fit within the ontogenetic range of Tyrannosaurus, that taxon would need to spend the first two decades of its life growing slowly before entering an abrupt plateau, and finally re-entering a lengthy growth phase—an ontogeny pattern not seen in any archosaur that contradicts skeletal fusion patterns observed in NCSM 40000.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli concluded that traits like tooth count variation are due to individual variation rather than ontogenetic plasticity.
facts.quote: Furthermore, they concluded that many of the traits commonly cited as ontogenetically plastic (i.e. variations in tooth count) were subject instead to individual variation.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli noted that the sinus obliteration required to merge Nanotyrannus and Tyrannosaurus has no precedent among living amniotes.
facts.quote: Further, they noted that certain traits, such as the "obliteration and resorption of a sinus" which would be necessary for Nanotyrannus and Tyrannosaurus to represent the same taxon, have no precedent among living amniotes.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli cited larger arm, wrist, and hand bones in Nanotyrannus compared to Tyrannosaurus as a distinguishing difference.
facts.quote: Bone proportions were another difference cited by Zanno and Napoli, as some of the arm, wrist, and hand bones of Nanotyrannus are larger than equivalent bones in Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli noted no known amniotes undergo absolute limb shrinkage, only proportional changes due to slower limb growth.
facts.quote: There are no amniotes known to the authors that undergo any degree of absolute limb shrinkage, merely instances where limbs grew slower than the rest of the body and became proportionally smaller.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists who previously questioned the validity of Nanotyrannus, including Thomas Carr, Steve Brusatte, and David Hone, accepted that the "Bloody Mary" specimen is a distinct species from Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Authors who have authored papers questioning Nanotyrannus validity, such as Thomas Carr, Steve Brusatte and David Hone, accepted that the "Bloody Mary" specimen was a distinct species from Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: After sampling the hyoids of the N. lancensis holotype, researchers concluded it belongs to a mature individual and is a species distinct from Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: After sampling the hyoids of the N. lancensis holotype, the researchers concluded that it belongs to a mature individual, and thus a species distinct from Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid

facts.statement: The holotype skull (CMNH 7541) of Nanotyrannus measures 57.2 cm from the anterior tip of the premaxilla to the posterior tip of the quadrate.
facts.quote: The holotype skull (CMNH 7541) of Nanotyrannus measures 57.2 cm when measured from the anterior (front) tip of the premaxilla to the posterior (rear) tip of the quadrate

facts.statement: The prominent subnarial foramen along the ventral extremity of the premaxilla-maxilla contact point is absent in every specimen of Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: this is absent in every specimen of Nanotyrannus

facts.statement: The quadratojugal and squamosal bones of Nanotyrannus form a long flange.
facts.quote: the quadratojugal and squamosal bones form a long flange

facts.statement: The basitubera of Nanotyrannus were strongly laterally expanded, suggesting the head could be strongly flexed sideways.
facts.quote: the basitubera (muscle attachment sites at the back of the head) of Nanotyrannus were strongly laterally expanded, suggesting that the head could be strongly flexed sideways

facts.statement: The lower jaw bone of Nanotyrannus has a rounded front edge.
facts.quote: The dentary of Nanotyrannus (the tooth-bearing bone of the lower jaw), has a rounded anterior margin.

facts.statement: Both species of Nanotyrannus lack chins, unlike the tyrannosaurid Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: The dentaries of both species lack chins, unlike tyrannosaurids such as Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Each front upper jaw bone of Nanotyrannus held four chisel-shaped teeth.
facts.quote: Each premaxilla bore four chisel-shaped teeth.

facts.statement: The upper jaw bones of Nanotyrannus held between fifteen and seventeen teeth, with the holotype having fifteen and N. lethaeus having sixteen per side.
facts.quote: The maxillae of Nanotyrannus have variable tooth counts: the holotype specimen preserves fifteen, NCSM 40000 has sixteen on the left maxilla and seventeen on the right maxilla, and N. lethaeus appears to have sixteen per maxilla.

facts.statement: The frontmost upper teeth of Nanotyrannus were small and similar to the front teeth, unlike in Daspletosaurus, Tarbosaurus, and Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Unlike Daspletosaurus, Tarbosaurus, and Tyrannosaurus, but like many other tyrannosauroids, the most anterior tooth of each maxilla was small and resembled those of the premaxillae.

facts.statement: The upper teeth of Nanotyrannus were ziphodont, which is different from most tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Unlike most tyrannosaurids, the maxillary teeth were ziphodont.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had between sixteen and eighteen lower jaw teeth, a higher count than any tyrannosaurid except Alioramus and Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus has between sixteen and eighteen teeth per dentary, a higher count than in any tyrannosaurid except for Alioramus and Daspletosaurus.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had approximately twenty neck vertebrae and thirty-five tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The vertebral column of Nanotyrannus appears to consist of twenty presacral vertebrae (those before the sacrum), and thirty-five caudal (tail) vertebrae.

facts.statement: The arms of Nanotyrannus were proportionally very large, resembling early tyrannosauroids more than later tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The arms of Nanotyrannus are proportionally very large, proportionally more similar to basal tyrannosauroids than to those of tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: The lower end of the upper arm bone of Nanotyrannus has five bumps, unlike other eutyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: The distal (further from the body) end of the humerus (upper arm bone) of Nanotyrannus bears five tubercles, unlike other eutyrannosaurs.

facts.statement: The hand of Nanotyrannus shares some features with albertosaurines but differs significantly from tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The manus (hand) is similar in some ways to albertosaurines, though it grossly differs in some regards from tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: The first finger bone of Nanotyrannus is nearly twice as large as the equivalent bone in Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: The first phalanx of the first manual digit is nearly twice the size of that of the equivalent bone in Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The hind legs of Nanotyrannus were proportionally much longer than those of other eutyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: The hind limbs of Nanotyrannus are proportionally very long compared to those of other eutyrannosaurs.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the long hind limbs of Nanotyrannus indicate a lifestyle adapted for chasing prey, unlike the ambush style of tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The extreme proportions of their "hypercursorial" hind limbs may correlate to a different lifestyle from tyrannosaurids, one adapted more toward pursuit predation.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the lack of serrations on Nanotyrannus teeth is due to age or a defining species trait, though they are likely diagnostic.
facts.quote: whilst the presence or absence of serrations has been suggested to vary with ontogeny, they are likely a diagnostic trait in the case of Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli hypothesized that the formation of the Western Interior Seaway caused the divergence of tyrannosaurids in Laramidia and nanotyrannids in Appalachia.
facts.quote: The formation of the seaway may have resulted in their divergence, with tyrannosaurids inhabiting the western island continent of Laramidia, and nanotyrannids inhabiting the eastern island continent of Appalachia.

facts.statement: Joseph Peterson and colleagues found healed puncture wounds on the skull of the Nanotyrannus holotype 'Jane', suggesting it was attacked by another juvenile Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Peterson and his team found that Jane's skull showed healed puncture wounds on the upper jaw and snout, which they believe came from another juvenile Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus was first discovered in the Hell Creek Formation, which spans parts of Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus was first discovered in the Hell Creek Formation, which spans parts of modern-day Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.

facts.statement: The Hell Creek Formation environment where Nanotyrannus was found was warm, humid, and swampy, reflecting maritime to subtropical conditions.
facts.quote: The depositional environment of this region was warm, humid, and swampy environment, reflecting maritime to subtropical conditions.

facts.statement: Average temperatures in the Hell Creek Formation environment ranged from 11.3 to 11.6 degrees Celsius.
facts.quote: The average temperatures ranged from 11.3 to 11.6 °C (52.3–52.9 °F).

facts.statement: Tyrannosaur teeth from the Ferris Formation originally described as Aublysodon have been reassigned to N. lancensis, with the youngest tooth found just below the K-Pg boundary.
facts.quote: Various tyrannosaur teeth from the Ferris Formation, originally described as Aublysodon, are reassigned to N. lancensis, with the stratigraphically youngest known tooth reported from a few meters below the K-Pg boundary zone.

facts.statement: The genus Nanotyrannus was named by Bakker, Currie, and Williams in 1988.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Bakker, Currie & Williams, 1988

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Nanotyrannus is Nanotyrannus lancensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Nanotyrannus lancencis

facts.statement: The type species Nanotyrannus lancensis was originally described by Gilmore in 1946.
facts.quote: type_species_authority: Gilmore, 1946

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lethaeus is a subdivision of the genus Nanotyrannus described by Zanno and Napoli in 2025.
facts.quote: subdivision: * Nanotyrannus lethaeus Zanno & Napoli, 2025

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lancensis has had several synonyms including Gorgosaurus lancensis, Deinodon lancensis, Aublysodon lancensis, Albertosaurus lancensis, and Tyrannosaurus lancensis.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Gorgosaurus lancensis Gilmore, 1946 Deinodon lancensis Gilmore, 1946 Aublysodon lancensis Gilmore, 1946 Albertosaurus lancensis Gilmore, 1946 Tyrannosaurus lancensis Gilmore, 1946

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 68 to 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage in North America.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus es un género extinto de dinosaurio terópodo tiranosauroide, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente de 68 a 66 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The genus name Nanotyrannus means "tiny tyrant" and contains two species: N. lancensis and N. lethaeus.
facts.quote: El nombre del género significa "tirano diminuto", y contiene dos especies: N. lancensis y N. lethaeus.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus is a medium-sized tyrannosaurid.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus es un tiranosauroide de tamaño mediano.

facts.statement: Adult N. lancensis may have weighed around 704 kg based on the Bloody Mary specimen.
facts.quote: El N. lancensis adulto pudo haber pesado alrededor de 704 kg, según el espécimen de Bloody Mary.

facts.statement: Adult N. lethaeus may have reached a body mass of approximately 1200 kg.
facts.quote: N. lethaeus, por su parte, era más grande; los individuos maduros pudieron haber alcanzado una masa corporal de aproximadamente 1200 kg.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus measured around 5.5 meters in length and 2 meters in height, about one-third the size of Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Solo medía alrededor de 5,5 metros de longitud y 2 de altura, un tercio del tamaño de Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had a flat, square head about 60 cm long, sharp claws and teeth, and a heavy body, typical of Cretaceous tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: En general tenía las características de cualquier tiranosáurido del Cretácico, una cabeza chata y cuadrada con un tamaño cercano a los 60 centímetros de largo, contaba con garras y dientes afilados, así como un cuerpo no liviano.

facts.statement: Bakker suggests that Nanotyrannus hunted in packs due to its weight and build.
facts.quote: Bakker sostiene que, debido a su peso y complexion, Nanotyrannus cazaba en manadas.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had a thin, low skull with small crests or horns just in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus tenía un cráneo delgado y bajo, y pequeñas crestas o cuernos justo delante de los ojos.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had non-serrated front upper teeth and laterally compressed rear teeth, a condition called ziphodonty not seen in tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Los dientes de la parte frontal de la mandíbula superior no eran serrados, a diferencia del resto, que a su vez se encontraban comprimidos lateralmente; condición conocida como zifodoncia que no se observa en los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had longer legs than contemporaries, suggesting it was a pursuit predator, and larger forelimbs both absolutely and proportionally than its relatives.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus tenía patas más largas que los taxones contemporáneos, lo que sugiere que era un depredador de persecución, y poseía extremidades anteriores que eran, tanto en términos absolutos como proporcionales, más grandes que las de sus parientes.

facts.statement: The exact implications of the difference in tooth number between Nanotyrannus and Tyrannosaurus have been controversial.
facts.quote: Las implicaciones exactas de esta diferencia en el número de dientes ha sido controvertida.

facts.statement: Carr used data showing tooth number decreases with development in Gorgosaurus to support the hypothesis that N. lancensis is simply a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Carr mostró que en Gorgosaurus libratus, el número de dientes decrecía conforme el animal se desarrollaba, y él usó estos datos para apoyar la hipótesis de que N. lancensis es simplemente un T. rex joven.

facts.statement: A team studying Tarbosaurus bataar found little to no reduction in tooth number during growth, even with very young specimens, supporting the idea that Nanotyrannus is a distinct genus.
facts.quote: El equipo de científicos que estudió el crecimiento en su pariente Tarbosaurus bataar encontró poca o ninguna reducción en el número de dientes en el crecimiento de la especie, incluso aunque disponían de especímenes mucho más jóvenes de lo que serían los de Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: Many differences cited to support Nanotyrannus validity are considered ontogenetic or individually variable traits.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, muchas de las diferencias que se citan para apoyar la validez de Nanotyrannus son rasgos ontogénica o individualmente variables.

facts.statement: In 2013, Carr declared that all differences supporting Nanotyrannus were individual traits, ontogenetic variables, or bone distortion products.
facts.quote: En 2013, Carr declaró que todas las diferencias que afirmaban apoyar a Nanotyrannus resultaron ser características individuales u ontogenéticamente variables o productos de distorsión de los huesos.

facts.statement: A 2016 limb proportion analysis suggested Nanotyrannus samples had different cursoriality levels, cited as a potential difference between N. lancensis and T. rex.
facts.quote: El análisis de proporción de extremidades publicado en 2016 sugirió que las muestras de Nanotyrannus tienen diferentes niveles de cursorialidad, citado como una diferencia potencial entre N. lancensis y T. rex.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered by Charles W. Gilmore in 1942 and described in 1946 as Gorgosaurus lancensis.
facts.quote: Representado por un pequeño cráneo, número de catálogo CMNH 7541, descubierto por Charles W. Gilmore en 1942 y descrito en 1946 como un espécimen de Gorgosaurus lancensis

facts.statement: The etymology of the name was later clarified to come from Greek words meaning 'dwarf' or 'pygmy' and 'king'.
facts.quote: Posteriormente se aclaró que la etimología proviene de las palabras griegas νάνος (nanos), que significa «enano» o «pigmeo», y τύραννος (tyrannos), que significa «rey»

facts.statement: Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky first suggested in 1965 that the holotype might represent a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: La posibilidad de que el holotipo representara un Tyrannosaurus rex juvenil fue sugerida por primera vez por Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky en 1965

facts.statement: Thomas Carr's detailed analysis in 1999 indicated that the specimen was indeed a juvenile.
facts.quote: Un detallado análisis del espécimen hecho por Thomas Carr en 1999 indicó que este espécimen era de hecho un juvenil

facts.statement: The debate intensified after the 2001 discovery of a new specimen nicknamed "Jane" (catalog number BMRP 2002.4.1).
facts.quote: especialmente desde el descubrimiento en 2001 de un nuevo espécimen de Nanotyrannus, apodado "Jane", número de catálogo BMRP 2002.4.1

facts.statement: A 2005 conference at the Burpee Museum of Natural History focused on the validity of Nanotyrannus as a genus.
facts.quote: En 2005, una conferencia sobre los tiranosáuridos, sostenida en el Museo de Historia Natural de Burpee, se enfocó en la validez del Nanotyrannus como género

facts.statement: Many paleontologists, including Phil Currie and Donald M. Henderson, concluded that Nanotyrannus was a juvenile T. rex or a closely related species.
facts.quote: Muchos paleontólogos, como Phil Currie y Donald M. Henderson, que examinaron a Jane concluyeron que el Nanotyrannus fue un T. rex juvenil o una especie muy cercana

facts.statement: Other researchers, such as Peter Larson, continue to support Nanotyrannus as a separate genus.
facts.quote: Otros, como Peter Larson, continúan apoyando un género separado para Nanotyrannus

facts.statement: A study by Bakker, Larson, and Currie aims to determine if Nanotyrannus is a distinct genus, a new species, or simply a young Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: El estudio científico de Jane, que publicarán Bakker, Larson, y Currie, puede ayudar a determinar si Nanotyrannus pertenece a un género propio, es un nuevo género y especie de tiranosáurido, o simplemente un Tyrannosaurus rex joven

facts.statement: Joshua David Schmerge proposed in a 2016 article that Nanotyrannus is a valid genus based on specimen BMRP 2002.4.1.
facts.quote: Joshua David Schmerge propuso en un artículo de 2016, que Nanotyrannus es un género válido basado en el espécimen BMRP 2002.4.1

facts.statement: Carr and associates argued in a separate document that the presence or absence of a tooth groove does not clarify the validity of Nanotyrannus or its phylogenetic position.
facts.quote: Carr y sus asociados escribieron un documento separado que afirmó que la presencia o ausencia de un surco dentario no aclara la validez de Nanotyrannus o su posición filogenética entre los tirannosauroides

facts.statement: The taxonomy of Nanotyrannus was complicated by the discovery of a small tyrannosaur near Jordan, Montana.
facts.quote: La taxonomía de Nanotyrannus se complicó aún más por el descubrimiento de un pequeño tiranosaurio cerca de Jordan, Montana

facts.statement: Molnar and Carpenter referred the Jordan theropod to Aublysodon.
facts.quote: Molnar y Carpenter refirieron el terópodo Jordan a Aublysodon

facts.statement: Stygivenator molnari is morphologically similar to the Nanotyrannus type, raising the possibility that it is a synonym of Nanotyrannus and thus also a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Stygivenator molnari es similar al tipo de Nanotyrannus en morfología general, lo que plantea la posibilidad de que sea sinónimo de Nanotyrannus, en cuyo caso también podría ser un T. rex juvenil

facts.statement: However, there are subtle and potentially significant differences in the shape of the teeth, maxillae, and dentaries.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, existen diferencias sutiles y potencialmente significativas en la forma de los dientes, maxilares y dentarios

facts.statement: In 2001, a more complete juvenile tyrannosaur nicknamed "Jane" (accession number BMRP 2002.4.1) was discovered and suggested to belong to the same species as the original Nanotyrannus specimen.
facts.quote: En 2001, se descubrió un tiranosaurio juvenil más completo (apodado "Jane", número de acceso BMRP 2002.4.1), que se sugirió pertenecía a la misma especie que el espécimen original de Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: Peter Larson continued to support the hypothesis that Nanotyrannus lancensis was a distinct but closely related species.
facts.quote: Peter Larson siguió apoyando la hipótesis de que Nanotyrannus lancensis era una especie distinta pero estrechamente relacionada

facts.statement: In late 2011, news reports covered the 2006 discovery of a nearly complete tyrannosaur specimen found alongside a ceratopsian.
facts.quote: A finales de 2011, se hicieron informes de noticias sobre el descubrimiento en 2006, de un nuevo espécimen de tiranosaurio prácticamente completo encontrado junto con un cerátopsido.

facts.statement: The specimen nicknamed "Bloody Mary" has arms that are nearly 3 feet long.
facts.quote: El espécimen, apodado "Bloody Mary", tiene brazos de casi 3 pies de largo

facts.statement: In 2020, the Montana Supreme Court ruled that ownership of the specimen should be granted to landowners Mary Anne and Lige Murray, who agreed to sell the fossils to a US museum.
facts.quote: En 2020, el Tribunal Supremo de Montana dictaminó que la propiedad del espécimen debía ser otorgada a los propietarios del terreno, Mary Anne y Lige Murray, quienes acordaron vender los fósiles a un museo estadounidense.

facts.statement: The North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences acquired the fossil in 2020.
facts.quote: El Museo de Ciencias Naturales de Carolina del Norte adquirió el fósil en 2020

facts.statement: They identified this specimen as a mature individual of Nanotyrannus and provided various evidence supporting the validity of the genus.
facts.quote: Identificaron este espécimen como un individuo de Nanotyrannus con el esqueleto maduro y aportaron diversas pruebas que respaldaban la validez de este género.

facts.statement: They also described a second species, N. lethaeus, based on the Jane specimen due to notable differences between it and N. lancensis.
facts.quote: También describieron una segunda especie, N. lethaeus, basándose en el espécimen Jane, debido a las notables diferencias entre este y N. lancensis.

facts.statement: The specific name lethaeus of the second species comes from Latin and is the adjective of Lethe, referring to the river Lethe of Greco-Roman mythology.
facts.quote: El nombre específico de la segunda especie, lethaeus, proviene del latín y es el adjetivo de Lete, en referencia al río Lete de la mitología grecorromana

facts.statement: The name alludes to the Hell Creek Formation, where the specimen was found, as well as the mythological function of drinking from the Lethe: forgetting a previous life and reincarnating.
facts.quote: El nombre alude tanto a la Formación Hell Creek, donde se encontró el espécimen, como a la función mitológica de beber del Lete: olvidar una vida anterior y reencarnarse.

facts.statement: Some scientists have defended the validity of Nanotyrannus lancensis based on the number of teeth.
facts.quote: La principal diferencia que algunos científicos han utilizado para defender la validez de Nanotyrannus lancensis radica en el número de dientes.

facts.statement: The implications of the difference in tooth number between Nanotyrannus and adult T. rex have not been universally accepted.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, las implicaciones exactas de esta diferencia en el número de dientes no han sido aceptadas universalmente.

facts.statement: The presence of a small foramen in the quadratojugal is another difference cited to support the validity of N. lancensis.
facts.quote: Otra diferencia citada en apoyo de la validez de N. lancensis es la presencia de un pequeño foramen en el cuadratoyugal.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Holly N. Woodward and colleagues indicated that specimens attributed to Nanotyrannus are ontogenetically immature and likely belong to Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2020 realizado por Holly N. Woodward y sus colegas indicó que los especímenes atribuidos a Nanotyrannus son ontogenéticamente inmaduros y halló probable que pertenecieran a Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: In 2024, Nicholas Longrich and Evan T. Saitta reexamined the holotype and referred specimens of Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: En 2024, Nicholas Longrich y Evan T. Saitta reexaminaron el holotipo y los especímenes referidos de Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: Longrich and Saitta concluded that the diversity of tyrannosaurids before the K-Pg extinction is greater than previously believed.
facts.quote: Por lo que la diversidad de tiranosáuridos antes de la extinción K-Pg es mayor de lo que se creía anteriormente.

facts.statement: In the same article, Zanno and Napoli concluded that another Nanotyrannus specimen, Jane (BMRP 2002.4.1), assigned to N. lethaeus, died between 8 and 14 years of age.
facts.quote: En el mismo artículo, Zanno y Napoli concluyeron que otro espécimen de Nanotyrannus , Jane (BMRP 2002.4.1), al que asignaron a N. lethaeus , murió entre los 8 y los 14 años de edad.

facts.statement: Zanno and Napoli noted that no known amniote undergoes absolute reduction of limbs, only cases where limbs grew more slowly than the rest of the body and became proportionally smaller.
facts.quote: Los autores no conocen ningún amniota que experimente algún grado de reducción absoluta de las extremidades, sino simplemente casos en los que las extremidades crecieron más lentamente que el resto del cuerpo y se volvieron proporcionalmente más pequeñas.

facts.statement: The article by Zanno and Napoli led some previously skeptical paleontologists to accept Nanotyrannus as a valid taxon.
facts.quote: El artículo de Zanno y Napoli ha llevado a algunos paleontólogos, antes escépticos respecto a Nanotyrannus, a aceptarlo como un taxón válido.

facts.statement: In 2025, Zanno and Napoli conducted two phylogenetic analyses using an extensive novel dataset focused on tyrannosauroid sampling.
facts.quote: En su artículo de 2025, Zanno y Napoli realizaron dos análisis filogenéticos utilizando un extenso conjunto de datos novedoso centrado en el muestreo de tiranosauroides.

facts.statement: Both analyses identified Nanotyrannus as a member of Eutyrannosauria within a new clade named Nanotyrannidae, which is the sister taxon to Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Ambos análisis identificaron a Nanotyrannus como miembro de Eutyrannosauria en un nuevo clado denominado Nanotyrannidae, que es el taxón hermano de Tyrannosauridae.

facts.statement: Therefore, it is only distantly related to derived tyrannosaurines such as Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, solo está lejanamente emparentado con tiranosaurinos derivados como Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: However, the exact resolution of taxa within Nanotyrannidae and their relationship differs between the two analyses.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la resolución exacta de los taxones dentro de Nanotyrannidae y en relación con ella difiere entre ambos análisis.

facts.statement: The authors noted that more evidence and data would be required to support the results of one analysis over the other.
facts.quote: Los autores señalaron que se requerirían más pruebas y datos para respaldar los resultados de un análisis sobre el otro.

facts.statement: Joseph Peterson and his colleagues found evidence of an intraspecific attack on Jane, which was at the time believed to be a juvenile Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Joseph Peterson y sus colegas hallaron evidencia de un ataque intraespecífico en Jane, que en ese entonces se creía que era una Tyrannosaurus juvenil.

facts.statement: It is believed that Nanotyrannus was significantly faster than an adult T. rex.
facts.quote: Se cree que Nanotyrannus era significativamente más rápido que un T. rex adulto.

facts.statement: In 2016, Scott Persons and Philip Currie calculated the cursorial limb proportion (CLP) of various theropod specimens, including Jane and the specimen "Bloody Mary" (then cataloged as BHI 6437), as an indicator to identify which theropod species had higher or lower running speeds.
facts.quote: En 2016, Scott Persons y Philip Currie calcularon la proporción de extremidades cursoriales (PEC) de varios especímenes de terópodos, incluyendo a Jane y el espécimen "Bloody Mary" (catalogado entonces como BHI 6437), como indicador para identificar qué especies de terópodos tenían mayor o menor velocidad de carrera.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus was found in the Hell Creek Formation, which covers parts of present-day Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus se encontró en la Formación Hell Creek, que abarca partes de los actuales Montana, Dakota del Sur, Dakota del Norte y Wyoming.

facts.statement: The sedimentary environment of this region was warm, humid, and swampy, reflecting maritime to subtropical conditions.
facts.quote: El ambiente de sedimentación de esta región era cálido, húmedo y pantanoso, lo que refleja condiciones marítimas a subtropicales.

facts.statement: Average temperatures ranged between 11.3 and 11.6 °C (52.3 and 52.9 °F).
facts.quote: Las temperaturas promedio oscilaron entre 11,3 y 11,6 °C (52,3 y 52,9 °F).

facts.statement: The landscape featured lush, low vegetation dominated by ferns, while the forest canopy consisted of a mix of various conifers (sequoias, cypresses, and pine-like trees) and angiosperms (flowering plants including sycamores, magnolia family members, laurels, various palms, and more).
facts.quote: El paisaje presentaba una vegetación exuberante y baja dominada por helechos, mientras que el dosel forestal consistía en una mezcla de diversas coníferas (secuoyas, cipreses y árboles parecidos a los pinos) y angiospermas (plantas con flores que incluían sicómoros, miembros de la familia de las magnolias, laureles, varias palmeras y más).

facts.statement: Wetlands and watercourses hosted diverse fauna. Small insects are known from the swampy forests, while rivers and lagoons were home to invertebrates (bivalves and ammonites), fish (sharks, hybodonts, catfish, and sturgeons), amphibians (frogs and salamanders), and various reptiles (turtles, crocodiles, the choristoderan Champsosaurus, and mosasaurs in coastal, brackish, and freshwater zones).
facts.quote: Los humedales y cursos de agua albergaban una fauna diversa. Se conocen pequeños insectos de lo que habrían sido los bosques pantanosos mientras que los ríos y lagunas eran hogar de invertebrados (bivalvos y amonites), peces (tiburones, hibodontes, catanes y esturiones), anfibios (ranas y salamandras) y diversos reptiles (tortugas, cocodrilos, el coristodero Champsosaurus y mosasaurios en las zonas costeras, salobres y de agua dulce).

facts.statement: Among non-avian theropods, in addition to Nanotyrannus, are the tyrannosaurid Tyrannosaurus, the ornithomimosaurians (Struthiomimus and Ornithomimus), the alvarezsaurid Trierarchuncus, the oviraptorosaurs (Anzu and Eoneophron), and the paravians Pectinodon (a troodontid) and Acheroraptor (a dromaeosaurid).
facts.quote: Entre los terópodos no avianos, además de Nanotyrannus, se incluyen el tiranosáurido Tyrannosaurus, los ornitomimosaurios (Struthiomimus y Ornithomimus), el alvarezsáurido Trierarchuncus, los oviraptorosaurios (Anzu y Eoneophron), y los paravianos Pectinodon (un trodóntido) y Acheroraptor (un dromaeosáurido).

facts.statement: Among avian dinosaurs are Avisaurus, Brodavis, and Magnusavis.
facts.quote: Entre los dinosaurios avianos se encuentran Avisaurus, Brodavis y Magnusavis.

facts.statement: Ornithischian dinosaurs include the ankylosaurians Ankylosaurus (an ankylosaurid) and Denversaurus (a nodosaurid), the neornithischian Thescelosaurus, the hadrosaurid Edmontosaurus, the pachycephalosaurs (Pachycephalosaurus, Platytholus, and Sphaerotholus), and the ceratopsians (Leptoceratops, Torosaurus, and Triceratops).
facts.quote: Los dinosaurios ornitisquios incluyen a los anquilosaurios Ankylosaurus (un anquilosáurido) y Denversaurus (un nodosáurido), el neornitisquio Thescelosaurus, el hadrosáurido Edmontosaurus, los paquicefalosaurios (Pachycephalosaurus, Platytholus y Sphaerotholus), y los ceratópsios (Leptoceratops, Torosaurus y Triceratops).
